pairs: Miserere nostri,
O God of all,
Deus omnium,
take pity on us,
et respice nos,
and look with favor on us,
et ostende nobis lucem miserationum tuarum:
and show us the light of your compassion.
et immitte timorem tuum super gentes quæ non exquisierunt te,
And send your fear upon the Gentiles, who have not sought you,
ut cognoscant quia non est deus nisi tu,
so that they may acknowledge that there is no God except you,
et enarrent magnalia tua.
and so that they may declare your great deeds.
Alleva manum tuam super gentes alienas,
Lift up your hand over unbelieving nations,
ut videant potentiam tuam.
so that they may see your power.
Sicut enim in conspectu eorum sanctificatus es in nobis,
For just as, in their sight, you have been sanctified in us,
sic in conspectu nostro magnificaberis in eis:
so also, in our sight, you will be magnified in them.
ut cognoscant te,
So may they know you,
sicut
as we also have known you.
et nos cognovimus quoniam non est deus præter te,
For there is no God apart from you,
Domine.
O Lord.
Innova signa,
Renew your signs,
et immuta mirabilia.
and work new wonders.
Glorifica manum et brachium dextrum.
Glorify your hand and your right arm.
Excita furorem,
Stir up your fury,
et effunde iram.
and pour out your wrath.
Tolle adversarium,
Take away our adversary,
et afflige inimicum.
and afflict our enemy.
Festina tempus,
Hasten the time,
et memento finis,
and remember the end,
ut enarrent mirabilia tua.
so that they may declare your miracles.
In ira flammæ devoretur qui salvatur:
Let those who escape be devoured by the wrath of fire.
et qui pessimant plebem tuam inveniant perditionem.
And let those who harass your people find perdition.
Contere caput principum inimicorum,
Crush the head of the leaders of the enemies,
dicentium:
for they say:
Non est alius præter nos.
“There is no other beside us.”
Congrega omnes tribus Jacob,
Gather together all the tribes of Jacob,
ut cognoscant quia non est deus nisi tu,
so that they may acknowledge that there is no God except you,
et enarrent magnalia tua,
and so that they may declare your great deeds.
et hæreditabis eos sicut ab initio.
And you will inherit them, as from the beginning.
Miserere plebi tuæ,
Take pity on your people,
super quam invocatum est nomen tuum,
over whom your name has been invoked,
et Israël quem coæquasti primogenito tuo.
and on Israel, whom you have treated as your firstborn.
Miserere civitati sanctificationis tuæ,
Take pity on Jerusalem,
Jerusalem,
the city of your sanctification,
civitati requiei tuæ.
the city of your rest.
Reple Sion inenarrabilibus verbis tuis,
Fill Zion with your ineffable words,
et gloria tua populum tuum.
and fill your people with your glory.
Da testimonium his qui ab initio creaturæ tuæ sunt,
Give testimony to those who have been your creations from the beginning,
et suscita prædicationes quas locuti sunt in nomine tuo prophetæ priores.
and lift up the prophecies which the former prophets spoke in your name.
Da mercedem sustinentibus te,
Give a reward to those who endure for you,
ut prophetæ tui fideles inveniantur:
so that your prophets may be found to be faithful.
et exaudi orationes servorum tuorum,
And heed the prayers of your servants,
secundum benedictionem Aaron de populo tuo:
in accord with the blessing of Aaron over your people.
et dirige nos in viam justitiæ,
And direct us in the way of justice,
et sciant omnes qui habitant terram quia tu es Deus conspector sæculorum.
and let all who inhabit the earth know that you are God, the Beholder of all ages.
Omnem escam manducabit venter:
The belly can devour any food,
et est cibus cibo melior.
yet one meal is better than another.
Fauces contingunt cibum feræ,
The palate tests the meat of wild animals,
et cor sensatum verba mendacia.
and the understanding heart tests false words.
Cor pravum dabit tristitiam,
A corrupt heart will cause grief,
et homo peritus resistet illi.
and a man of experience will resist it.
Omnem masculum excipiet mulier:
A woman can receive any male,
et est filia melior filia.
yet one daughter is better than another.
Species mulieris exhilarat faciem viri sui,
The beauty of a wife cheers the face of her husband,
et super omnem concupiscentiam hominis superducit desiderium.
and rises above his desire, above all the desires of man.
Si est lingua curationis,
If she offers healing words,
est et mitigationis et misericordiæ:
then she both comforts and shows mercy;
non est vir illius secundum filios hominum.
and so her husband is not like other men.
Qui possidet mulierem bonam inchoat possessionem:
He who holds to a good wife establishes a possession.
adjutorium secundum illum est,
She is a helper in agreement with him,
et columna ut requies.
and she is a pillar of rest.
Ubi non est sepes,
Where there is no hedge,
diripietur possessio:
a possession will be trampled.
et ubi non est mulier,
And where there is no wife,
ingemiscit egens.
he will mourn her absence.
Quis credit ei qui non habet nidum,
Who will trust one who has no nest,
et deflectens ubicumque obscuraverit,
and who conceals himself wherever his course may take him,
quasi succinctus latro exiliens de civitate in civitatem?
like a well-equipped robber passing from city to city?
